content_voiceover: This slide gets into the practical mechanics of phenotype-matched red cell release. The core principle, just as you match ABO type for compatibility, minor blood group antigens should also be matched according to the same compatibility rule. Locally, the recommended minor antigen panel covers six antigens, E, e, C, c, Jka, and Jkb, worth memorizing as the core extended panel tested on boards. There's also an important point about RhD itself, current practice already treats RhD as a phenotype-matched strategy, not just a simple positive-or-negative call. Specifically, RhD-negative patients should only receive RhD-negative red cells, while RhD-positive patients can safely receive either RhD-positive or RhD-negative units. Finally, notice that blood bags are labeled with their minor antigen phenotype directly on the bag, as shown in the image, a label might read something like C plus, c negative, E negative, e plus, M plus, Jka plus, Jkb negative. Having this printed directly on the unit is what makes rapid antigen-matched release feasible in practice, without waiting for additional serologic workup on every unit.
keypoints: Minor blood group antigens are matched using the same compatibility principle as ABO
Core recommended minor antigen panel is E, e, C, c, Jka, Jkb
RhD-negative patients get only RhD-negative units; RhD-positive patients can receive either
Blood bags are labeled with minor antigen phenotype to speed antigen-matched release
